nodes.label: quicKFS Wire Protocol Specification v6.4
nodes.rationale: Normative for a second implementation or an audit; crates/protocol/src/lib.rs is the canonical source of truth and wins any disagreement.

nodes.label: Length-Prefixed Frame Layout
nodes.rationale: A 4-byte big-endian prefix whose high bit is FRAME_COMPRESSED_FLAG and whose low 31 bits are the body length. Because a real length never reaches bit 31 (MAX_FRAME_SIZE is 1 MiB) the flag can never collide with a length, and a receiver must reject an over-large declared length before allocating.

nodes.label: Postcard Positional Serialization
nodes.rationale: Postcard is compact but non-self-describing: struct fields are positional with no names or count and enum variants are identified by declaration-order index. There is no tolerance for a missing or extra trailing field and #[serde(default)] does not rescue a shortened struct on the wire, which is exactly why every compatibility rule below exists.

nodes.label: Metadata Wire Record
nodes.rationale: Field order is wire order and must not change. There is deliberately no distinct ctime field: adding one is a positional struct change Postcard cannot carry compatibly within a major.

nodes.label: Raw I/O Bodies
nodes.rationale: ReadRange/GetXattr responses and WriteRange/SetXattr requests state a byte count then send exactly that many raw bytes on the same stream, never compressed at this layer because file bytes are typically already-compressed media.

nodes.label: ErrorCode Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Codes map to the platform adapter's native errno (NotFound->ENOENT, TooLarge->EFBIG, Conflict/InvalidNode->ESTALE); UnsupportedVersion is returned uncompressed when a peer's major differs from 6.

nodes.label: Major.Minor Version Negotiation
nodes.rationale: The version word packs major in the high byte and minor in the low byte of a u16. The ALPN is keyed to the major only (quickfs/6) so every 6.x peer still connects instead of failing at the TLS handshake; per-request checks accept any same-major minor and hard-reject only a different major. Each peer learns the other's exact version (client from HelloAck, server from every request envelope) so the server holds no per-connection version state.

nodes.label: peer_supports_<feature> Capability Gating
nodes.rationale: A peer emits an optional feature only when the partner advertises support at or above the feature's floor minor, so a newer peer withholds what an older same-major peer cannot parse and no flag day is needed.

nodes.label: Guideline: Adding a Protocol Version
nodes.rationale: Add never reshape: append new enum variants at the end, never insert/reorder/remove; never change an existing struct's field count, order, or type; gate emission on negotiation with a MINOR_<FEATURE> floor and predicate; self-describing frame flags may be decoded unconditionally but setting them is still negotiated; bump PROTOCOL_MINOR and record it; prove all four old/new client x server combinations in tests. A change that cannot obey these is a major bump, which changes the ALPN and is a genuine flag day. There is no intermediate 'breaking but same-ALPN' tier until a per-major capability bitset lands.

nodes.label: Known Non-Additive Changes
nodes.rationale: Distinct ctime on Metadata (a positional field on a struct embedded in ~a dozen responses) and server-initiated push (a transport-shaped change, not an enum append) are deferred precisely because they cannot be compatible minors.

nodes.label: Ambiguous Mutation Non-Retry Rule
nodes.rationale: A mutation's outcome after a transport failure may already have taken effect, so it is never blindly retried (AmbiguousMutation, mapped to EIO). Safe reads and lookups may reconnect and retry; a handle is reopened only when the persistent epoch and exact file revision still match.
